On the heels of announcing its endorsement of Vacaville mayoral and city council candidates, the Vacaville Chamber of Commerce has announced its support of Measure V, a proposed one-cent local sales tax increase that local voters will decide on the Nov. 3 ballot. In announcing its support, the chamber said in a press release that it does not take this position lightly. “As an organization representing Vacaville’s business community, the Chamber has historically approached tax increases with significant caution,” the chamber noted. “As a general principle, we do not support tax increases or other measures that unnecessarily increase the cost of doing business or add to the cost of living for Vacaville residents.” The Chamber said Vacaville’s current financial situation represents a change in circumstances, citing the city’s structural budget deficit and the need to consider its long-term financial stability. “After reviewing the city’s fiscal outlook, the projected structural budget deficit, and the potential consequences for essential municipal services, the Chamber believes Measure V is a necessary step toward addressing Vacaville’s current financial challenges,” the Chamber said in its announcement. Measure V would impose an additional one-cent local sales tax and is expected to generate an estimated $28 million annually, according to the Chamber. The organization said the revenue would remain under local control and could be used for services including police, fire and emergency response, street and infrastructure maintenance, parks and recreation, and economic development. The Chamber said a financially stable city is important to the local business community, pointing to the need for safe neighborhoods and commercial districts, reliable emergency services, well-maintained infrastructure, and effective economic development. At the same time, it said additional revenue should not be the only response to the city’s financial challenges. Its support comes with an expectation of “accountability, fiscal discipline, transparency, and continued efforts by city government to control expenditures,” the Chamber said. It also called for continued efforts to identify efficiencies, control unnecessary spending, establish sustainable financial practices, and make measurable progress toward a balanced long-term budget. The Chamber also pointed to accountability provisions in Measure V, such as independent annual financial audits, public reporting, and citizen oversight. “Supporting Measure V does not represent a change in the Chamber’s general philosophy regarding taxation,” the organization said. “Rather, it reflects our assessment of the specific financial circumstances facing Vacaville today and the importance of protecting the services and infrastructure necessary for a strong local economy.” The Chamber said it intends to remain engaged in monitoring the city’s fiscal progress and advocating for responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars. “Vacaville’s businesses and residents share an interest in a city that is safe, financially stable, economically competitive, and positioned for future growth,” the announcement reads. “The Chamber believes addressing the City’s structural budget challenges — while simultaneously demanding greater fiscal responsibility — is important to achieving that objective.” Subscribers are entitled to 10 gift sharing articles each month. title: GM's New 6.6-Liter V-8 Beats Ford Where It Counts Most - HotCars
content: Subscribe to the HotCars newsletter to never miss an update GM dropped the full engine specs for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 on September 17, and the headline writes itself: both V-8s got bigger. The outgoing 5.3-liter is gone, replaced by a 5.7-liter making 402 horsepower and 428 lb-ft of torque — 47 hp and 45 lb-ft more than what it replaces. Above it sits the new 6.6-liter, pumping out 481 hp and 501 lb-ft, which makes these trucks the most powerful naturally aspirated pickups on the market. Both engines are built on the sixth-generation small-block architecture that debuted in the 2027 Corvette's 6.7-liter LS6, but tuned specifically for towing, hauling, and off-road use rather than track duty. The displacement gains aren't just a spec-sheet flex — they translate directly into towing capacity that edges out Ford's best EcoBoost numbers. Truck buyers who've been skeptical of downsizing trends at rival brands finally have a V-8 argument worth making. The smaller of the two new V-8s carries the RPO code L76 and displaces a heritage-steeped 350 cubic inches — the same number that's been sacred in GM's small-block lineage for decades. GM stretched the stroke by 6.0 millimeters to get there, and the result is an engine that nearly matches the outgoing 6.2-liter's output while slotting in as the base V-8. More importantly for work-truck buyers, the 5.7 is the towing king of the lineup. Properly configured — Silverado Double Cab, rear-wheel drive — it pulls up to 13,700 pounds. That's 200 pounds more than the 2027 Ford F-150 with the 3.5-liter EcoBoost V-6, which tops out at 13,500. The     Sierra 1500 with the 5.7 matches Ford at 13,500 pounds. The bigger 6.6-liter, by contrast, is paired with higher-trim configurations that carry more weight and consequently drop the tow rating to 9,700 pounds in the Silverado. The L78 6.6-liter replaces the 6.2 and represents GM's performance flagship for the half-ton segment. At 481 hp and 501 lb-ft, it outpaces the F-150's 5.0-liter Coyote V-8 (400 hp, 410 lb-ft) and the EcoBoost 3.5-liter (400 hp, 500 lb-ft) on both metrics — though     Ford's PowerBoost hybrid counters with 430 hp and 570 lb-ft if you want to count electrified assistance. Ram's high-output Hurricane inline-six (540 hp, 521 lb-ft) still leads on raw numbers, but that's a force-fed six, not a naturally aspirated V-8. The L78 is not the same engine as the     Corvette 's LS6, despite sharing the Gen 6 architecture and the same 4.40-inch bore spacing. GM small-block design systems engineer Randy Dufresne confirmed to Road & Track that the truck engine's compression ratio sits at 12.5:1 — significantly up from the 6.2's 11.5:1, but deliberately kept below the Corvette's 13.0:1 to suit truck duty cycles. The 6.6 carries a premium-recommended fuel designation, but GM does not require it. Both V-8s share a set of significant engineering upgrades. Throttle body diameter grows from 87 mm to 95 mm — the same size used in the Corvette — and completely redesigned intake manifolds with tuned runners manage the increased airflow. Fueling moves from exclusive direct injection to a combined port-and-direct system, which GM says improves power, efficiency, and emissions simultaneously. The oiling system received the most thorough redesign. A continuously variable displacement oil pump delivers flow and pressure on demand rather than protecting for worst-case loads at all times, reducing parasitic loss. An on-engine oil cooler and enlarged lifter galleries are also part of the package, along with dual main feeds to the main bearings. GM engineers specifically noted that every oil passage was machined for cleanliness to eliminate residual casting sand — a pointed acknowledgment of the rod-bearing failures that plagued the outgoing 6.2-liter. Recommended viscosity steps up to 0W-30 from 0W-20. One side effect of the new port injection hardware and revised packaging: there's no room for a traditional oil dipstick. Both V-8s use a digital oil-level readout in the cabin instead, a feature that's already common on German brands but will likely generate some grumbling from the truck crowd. The 2.7-liter TurboMax four-cylinder carries over but gets a meaningful upgrade — new turbo, revised fuel injection, redesigned pistons, and improved thermal management push output to 350 hp and 455 lb-ft, gains of 40 hp and 25 lb-ft over the 2026 version. That torque figure actually tops the 5.7-liter V-8, and the four-cylinder leads the entire lineup in payload capacity at 2,340 pounds for the Silverado. It also moves to the 10-speed automatic shared with all other engines, dropping the old eight-speed. The Duramax 3.0-liter turbodiesel carries over largely unchanged at 305 hp and 495 lb-ft, but gains updates to pistons, turbo vane, NOx sensor, and fuel injectors. A new optional 34-gallon fuel tank pairs with the diesel for an estimated highway range of over 900 miles on a full tank. Production of the new V-8s will be split across three GM facilities: Flint Engine Operations, Tonawanda Propulsion in New York, and St. Catharines Propulsion in Canada. Both engines will be available at the Silverado and Sierra's late-2026 launch. Pricing has not been announced. For truck buyers who've watched GM's rivals lean harder into turbo sixes and hybrid assist, the 5.7 and 6.6 are a clear statement: displacement still wins arguments in the half-ton segment. Whether the new oiling architecture puts the reliability concerns of the 6.2 era firmly in the rearview mirror is the question every prospective buyer should be watching when these trucks hit dealerships. Black Ferns: 66 (Mo'omo'oga Palu, Maama Vaipulu, Justine McGregor, Elinor-Plum King, Layla Sae two, Amy Du Plessis, Amarante Sititi, Tara Turner, Alena Saili tries; Braxton Sorensen-McGee seven con, Hannah King con)Scotland: 14 (Evie Gallagher two tries; Helen Nelson two cons)HT: 38-14 The Black Ferns achieved their highest score against Scotland since 1998 despite scoring only one try in the last 33 minutes. The bench emptied and debuts were awarded to Manawatū duo Ngano Tavake and Maia Davis. Davis immediately retreated to make a try-saving tackle on centre Rachel Philipps. Tavake won a scrum penalty with her first hit. The Black Ferns settled the contest with two scoring bursts at the start of each half. Two tries were scored in the first eight minutes; three in the first seven after halftime. The Black Ferns started with precision, speed and intensity Scotland couldn't match. Tighthead prop Mo'omo'oga Palu clattered through two tackles and burst 20 metres for her first Test try during the Black Ferns' first trip to the hosts' 22. Six minutes later the Black Ferns struck again. Flanker Mia Anderson drew in two with a hard carry and lock Maama Vaipulu barged clear. Vaipulu had 11 carries and was the Black Ferns' top defender with 20 tackles, three turnovers and two lineout steals. In the 19th minute, an intercept by Scottish fullback Chloe Rollie changed momentum. Scotland soared into the Black Ferns 22 and muscled over for their first try through No.8 Evie Gallagher. Scotland could have had another shortly after. Second five-eighth Meryl Smith, in her 29th Test, busted and booted ahead where there was no fullback. Unfortunately, the ball blew dead, and instead the Black Ferns had a scrum 10 inside Scottish territory. Phases were built swiftly, and with a delightful pivot and pass, hooker Georgia Ponsonby opened a hole for centre Amy Du Plessis, who in turn provided winger Justine McGregor for her third try in six Tests. The Black Ferns' best try came after 29 minutes. Five passes inside the 22 saw winger Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a (three linebreaks) burst 50 metres with Elinor-Plum King (15 carries, 13 tackles) trailing on the inside to complete the easy run in. Smith was the liveliest of the Scottish backs and her break enabled Gallagher to battle ahead for a second in the 32nd minute. Gallagher has 14 tries in 45 Tests. She topped the tackle count with 24, two ahead of 21-year-old lock Holland Bogan. Normal transmission resumed in the 35th minute with a Layla Sae (13 carries, 11 tackles) try. The Hurricanes Poua flanker has returned from a long-term injury with vigour. Du Plessis had the last say of the first half supporting another Anderson break. There was no respite for Scotland after the break, with tries to Amarante Sititi, player of the match, halfback Tara Turner and a second for Sae. A combination of power and swift handling created the holes. Scotland missed 47 tackles compared to the Black Ferns 16. The final half hour lost some shape as new combinations were tried and the heavens opened. Black Ferns coach Whitney Hansen was delighted the newer players "owned their roles." She's thrilled there is a challenge for spots. The Black Ferns can top the WXV Global Series standings for the first time with a draw against England at Twickenham next Saturday. The Red Roses and Canada shared a 26-26 draw at Sandy Park in Exeter. For Rugby World Champions England, it's their worst result since losing to the Black Ferns 34-31 in the 2022 Rugby World Cup Final. England are unbeaten in their last 40 internationals with 39 wins and a draw. France edged Australia 29-26 despite two red cards, at one stage being reduced to 12 players. The Black Ferns have won 122 of 147 Tests. That includes eight in a row and all five internationals against Scotland, outscoring the Scots 250-23. New Zealand won the first Black Ferns-Scotland Test 76-0 at the 1998 Rugby World Cup in Amsterdam. Annaleah Bodle (nee Rush) scored 17 points. At the 2022 Rugby World Cup in Whangārei, the Black Ferns beat Scotland 57-0. Renee Holmes scored 22 points.

title: Susanna Fletcher Greer: How V Foundation Scholars Are Reshaping Pediatric Cancer Care - Oncodaily
content: Susanna Fletcher Greer, Chief Scientific Officer at the V Foundation, shared on LinkedIn: This week, I want to share a the V Foundation funded study that matters because it points to a new way of thinking about a childhood cancer that still has far too few treatment options. Rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents. It develops from cells that are meant to become muscle, and some forms of the disease can be especially aggressive. For children whose cancer has already spread at diagnosis, five-year survival remains dismally low; below 20 percent. For these children and their families, we urgently need new ideas that can lead to better treatments; and this is one of them. The work involves three V Foundation funded investigators at Duke, Drs. Kris Wood, Christine Eyler and Corinne Linardic, and offers one of those desperately needed ideas. The team focused on a form of rhabdomyosarcoma driven by a genetic change that keeps immature muscle cells from developing normally and instead pushes them to keep growing as cancer cells. That genetic driver has been very difficult to target directly, so the researchers asked a different question. ‘Instead of trying to attack the cancer at its source, could they find something the cancer had become dependent on in order to survive?’ These cancer cells rely heavily on a protein called FANCM to help manage the stresses created by the very changes that are driving the cancer. In some ways, the cancer creates its own problem...and then becomes dependent on FANCM to help it cope. When the researchers removed FANCM, the cancer cells could no longer maintain the same aggressive growth program. The cells grew more slowly, and remarkably, they began to move back toward a more normal muscle cell state. In animal models, disrupting FANCM also slowed tumor growth and improved survival. Exciting results. Super promising! This is not yet a FANCM targeted treatment ready for children with rhabdomyosarcoma; but what this study gives us is something earlier in the drug development process: a new weakness to pursue in a cancer that has been very difficult to treat. It also gives drug developers a clearer place to focus their efforts, which is how basic discovery begins to move toward patient impact. I have to say what I also love about this study is that it brings together three V Foundation funded investigators, Drs. Wood, Eyler and Linardic. ‘It’s so meaningful to see scientists we have chosen to support come together around a difficult problem, because it reinforces the importance of investing in exceptional people as well as exceptional projects.’ The impact of a grant can extend far beyond the work originally proposed when talented investigators become part of a broader scientific community and begin building on one another’s ideas. For me, this study matters so much because it gives the field a new direction. And for families facing a cancer where progress has been too slow and options remain too limited, every new direction matters. title: CR-V Is Destroying RAV4 In America, And Honda Is About To Turn Up The Heat - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update Toyota's new, all-hybrid RAV4 line should've been dominating the sales charts this year. It packed fresh styling, more power, and more efficiency in what was already America's favorite vehicle that wasn't an F-Series. Instead, production woes sent sales plummeting early in the year. That's left an opening for its fiercest rival, the Honda CR-V to overtake it. In fact, the Honda is so far ahead, it's unlikely that Toyota can catch up this year. It seems Honda is wanting to hold onto that lead, since it may be launching a new generation of CR-V even earlier than expected. We've known for some time now that Honda has been working up a revised platform and powertrain for its small to midsize hybrids, which include the Civic, CR-V, and Accord. Honda shared details and even demonstrated a test car late last year. At that time, we were expecting to see either a new hybrid Civic or CR-V appear toward the end of 2026. It now seems certain that the CR-V is probably what we'll see, since Japanese news outlet Nikkei reports that production of the new CR-V hybrid will start in Canada in February, followed by its plants in Indiana and Ohio in March. That probably means vehicles arriving at dealers before summer. This new CR-V hybrid will likely be substantially different from the current model, which is a bit of a surprise considering the current one has only been around since the 2023 model year. The big differences will come from the new chassis, which will be lighter and up to 10% cheaper to produce, as well as the updated powertrain. While it will still use a naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder, it will have some improvements to efficiency from direct fuel injection and new electric motors. Honda is also adding the simulated shifting from the Prelude, some interesting power control tricks to aid handling, and, apparently, a surprisingly sporty exhaust note. Ultimately, the Toyota RAV4 may return to glory, especially once the company finally gets production back up to full pace. However, if the new CR-V hybrid delivers on efficiency and cost improvements on top of its great driving dynamics, Toyota should be worried about losing sales. Even worse, though, is that a new Honda won't be the only thing for the RAV4 to face down. Nissan is about to launch its first hybrid Rogue in years. It's on a completely new platform that will eventually be joined by a combustion-only version in the near future, and our experience with a prototype shows that it has serious potential in the segment. Hyundai has also revealed a completely new Tucson for next year with stand-out styling and it's notably bigger. Depending on how these new models perform, the RAV4, which is a heavily refreshed version of its predecessor, could suddenly be at a disadvantage, right as production starts picking up. Aside from Toyota having some real reasons to worry about the RAV4's position in the compact SUV segment, Honda moving up CR-V production, and especially the hybrid, says something else. It shows how important hybrids are becoming in the market. Even Nissan has prioritized getting the hybrid version of its new Rogue to market before the combustion one. It's also quite possible that demand for hybrids could grow even more now that gas prices are spiking. In fact, Toyota probably isn't the only company that should be concerned about its position in the car market, but so should American automakers that are lacking small hybrid SUVs. title: Fulham v Man Utd: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Manchester United travel to Fulham on Sunday with both sides in desperate need of a win going into the lengthy international break. The Red Devils, who were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton on Wednesday, have won just one of their opening four Premier League games this season to leave them 13th, already eight points adrift of the early pace-setters Arsenal and Manchester City. The Brighton defeat rounded off a difficult few days for United head coach Michael Carrick, whose side were insipid in the Manchester derby loss to 10-man City last Sunday. Throw in the uncertainty over academy star JJ Gabriel's future and Carrick is in dire need of three points on the road in west London. The good news for him is that United's recent record against Fulham is outstanding; they have lost just once in the past 21 league meetings between the two sides, winning 16 and drawing four. The only out-and-out centre-forward at Carrick's disposal, Benjamin Sesko, has been used as a substitute in the four league games so far, scoring once off the bench against Everton. With his team drawing blanks in two of those four games, there are calls for the Slovenia striker to start at Craven Cottage, having netted a stoppage-time winner against the same opposition at Old Trafford last season. The Red Devils have had more shots than any other top-flight side across the first four matchdays of this season, but aren't among the division's top four scorers. So far, only Brighton (10.2) have accumulated a higher xG than United's 8.3. Although Sesko struggled to make an impact midweek against Brighton, he is fully recovered from the shin injury he sustained in early May, so Carrick may turn to the club's joint-top scorer from last season in the hope he can convert some of the many shots United are creating. Winless Fulham find themselves in the relegation zone after four games, with new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa cursing his luck just two months into the job. The Spaniard's side, currently 18th, were booed off at Craven Cottage after a third successive league defeat against Crystal Palace on 5 September. All three have come via a one-goal margin. A draw against Liverpool at Anfield last Saturday and a 3-2 midweek win over West Ham United in the EFL Cup have given the Fulham faithful some cause for optimism, though - as has Josh King's continued good form. King, still only 19, is the Cottagers' top league scorer with two goals and the Londoner has his sights set on a senior England call-up this season. He was one of four youngsters to feature in Thomas Tuchel's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, along with Alex Scott, Rio Ngumoha and Ethan Nwaneri. Since the start of last season, when he cemented his place in the Fulham side, the only teenager to make more appearances than King in Europe's top five leagues is Yan Diomande, who joined Real Madrid from RB Leipzig for an initial fee of £107m last month. On 1 February, the last time the two teams met, late goals from Raul Jimenez and Kevin threatened to earn Fulham a point, before Benjamin Sesko's late winner. That result triggered a worrying collapse in form – since then, the only ever-present side in the division to win fewer points than Fulham are Tottenham. It is a rut Arbeloa must urgently get out of.

title: Man City v Sunderland: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Manchester City will look to maintain their 100% league record under Enzo Maresca when they welcome Sunderland to Etihad Stadium on Sunday. Maresca's tenure got off to a wobbly start with the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal, but his troops have rallied to ensure they are level on points with the table-topping Gunners at this early stage, trailing only on goal difference. In fact, the Italian is aiming to become just the sixth manager to win his first five Premier League games in charge of a club. The Blues, last season's runners-up, are on a mightily impressive run of league form, having lost just two of their past 30 matches, winning 20 and drawing eight. Their record at home to the Black Cats is also enviable. City are unbeaten in all 14 of their Premier League home games against Sunday's opposition, winning 12 of those encounters. Sunderland's last league win in this fixture came at Maine Road in the second tier in January 1998. Erling Haaland, Golden Boot winner in three of his four campaigns in England, is already the pace-setter for this season's prize with four goals. Sunderland, however, are the only top-flight team he has faced without scoring. The Norwegian has scored in eight of his past nine league appearances, netting nine goals. In two games against the Black Cats, he had had three shots with an xG of 0.75 without finding the net. Don't bet against him breaking his duck on Sunday. Juggling Sunderland's European commitments with their domestic schedule was always going to be one of the biggest tasks facing Regis le Bris this season. Having got their Europa League campaign off to a winning start against AZ Alkmaar on Wednesday – the club's first game in continental competition since 1973 – the Black Cats must focus on climbing the Premier League table after an unconvincing start. Four points from four games has them sitting 14th, and history suggests this won't be the fixture to propel them up the table. The Black Cats haven't won any of their past 17 top-flight games against teams starting the day in the top two, losing 13 and drawing four. Couple that with the fact they are winless in nine league games against Manchester City – since a 1-0 home victory under Gus Poyet in November 2013 – and it looks like a tall order for Le Bris' side to head back to Wearside with all three points. Something for Sunderland to cling to, however, is the fact they have scored in each of their past eight league away games, their best run of scoring on the road in this competition since another run of eight in 2015-16. The atmosphere at the Stadium of Light against AZ was electric and Le Bris is keen for that feelgood factor to continue. It is a demanding schedule for his squad, though they will have an extra day's rest over City, who battered Norwich 5-0 in the Carabao Cup on Thursday. "It is a tough week but it is exactly what we want to do," the Frenchman said.

title: V Girls: Arrow de Wilde is Taking Aim at Rock’s Status Quo - V Magazine
content: Arrow De Wilde keeps rock’s rebellious streak alive as Starcrawler takes aim at what comes next. Arrow De Wilde keeps rock’s rebellious streak alive as Starcrawler takes aim at what comes next. Rejections of the status quo run through punk’s history. Its spirit remains alive and well, too–in Arrow De Wilde, the lead singer of LA-based band Starcrawler. De Wilde grew up surrounded by creativity. As the daughter of a drummer dad and a photographer mom, De Wilde’s early years were spent at concerts, in studios, and with musicians talking about a shared love for sonic rebellion. Accordingly, she lists Johnny Thunders, Cheap Trick, Hanoi Rocks, and Redd Kross as influences. De Wilde’s exposure to art was not limited to music, however–De Wilde also cites horror movies like The Texas Chain Saw Massacre as a key source of inspiration for her performances. Starcrawler’s story begins at De Wilde’s Los Angeles high school. Knowing she wanted to start a band, De Wilde kept her eyes peeled in the halls, until one day she saw Henri Cash, with his long hair and leather jacket. “I didn’t know him but I went up to him and just said, ‘you look cool, do you play guitar?’” De Wilde said. “And luckily he did!” De Wilde and Cash began bringing on other members, eventually forming Starcrawler in 2015. Since releasing their debut song, “Ants,” in 2017, they have carried with them an unapologetic confidence and undeniable flair. People have taken notice, including Elton John and My Chemical Romance’s Gerard Way. They’ve retained their sense of individuality the whole time. “I think this goes for any genre of music: if it’s truly what you love and what comes natural to you and you don’t have to overthink it, then it’s what is meant to be,” De Wilde says. “Writing a rock song is pretty much all I know how to do (at least right now), so it’s the music that I make. I think when people try to force something that’s not actually true to themselves is when a lot of shitty music gets made.” Touring the country this fall, Starcrawler wants to show audiences what they’ve got. Fake blood, loud screams, and thrashing energy are the expectations of a Starcrawler show, and yes, they deliver. “To us it’s all about having a good time, writing and playing music that we love, putting on a good live show for others, and just hopefully creating special memories not just for us, but also for the people that like and support us and our music,” said De Wilde. Starcrawler’s latest single, “ON 2 U” is out now on all major streamers. The time for Starcrawler is now because, in the words of Arrow De Wilde herself, “life is just too damn short!” This cover story appears in the pages of V162: now available for purchase! title: Behind the Wheel: Budget SUVs – Honda HR-V vs. Kia Seltos - Toledo Blade
content: Crossovers have become a popular choice for buyers who want the practicality of an SUV without the size and expense of a larger vehicle. For many shoppers, that means finding a vehicle that’s easy to live with, offers enough room for everyday duties, keeps fuel costs in check, and provides the versatility to be useful for a range of needs. The 2027 Honda HR-V and 2027 Kia Seltos both make a case for that balance, but they take somewhat different approaches to the formula. Honda’s HR-V is the little sibling to the larger CR-V and sets a benchmark for what to expect from an extra-small SUV. Kia’s Seltos is less well known but enters 2027 with a full redesign that brings more space, revamped styling and a newly available hybrid powertrain. Both are compelling options, but which one is the better buy? Edmunds put these two SUVs head-to-head to find out. Both the Kia Seltos and Honda HR-V make good use of their compact dimensions, offering roomy cabins with generous space in both rows. The Seltos has an especially accommodating rear seat, even for taller passengers. Easy-access child seat anchors add to its family-friendly appeal. For a small SUV like this, the Seltos also boasts a reasonably smooth ride over bumps. The HR-V is similarly roomy, with large door openings and a comfortable seat height that make entry and exit a breeze. It also has a pretty smooth ride. But Edmunds noticed a difference in seat comfort between these two SUVs. The HR-V’s overly firm front seat cushions and lack of lumbar adjustment take a toll on long-distance comfort. If you frequently have rear passengers, the Seltos has another advantage by way of its rear air vents. You don’t get them in the HR-V. Neither the 158-horsepower Honda HR-V nor the 147-horsepower Kia Seltos is quick off the line. In Edmunds’ testing, the HR-V needed 10.2 seconds to get from zero to 60 mph, while the Seltos posted a 10.6-second run to 60 mph. Thankfully, you can get a Seltos with a more powerful 190-horsepower turbocharged engine that livens up the car’s acceleration. The HR-V is only available with its base engine. Both SUVs can deliver impressive fuel economy. The EPA estimates that the HR-V will get up to 28 mpg in combined city/highway driving. The Seltos gets up to an estimated 30 mpg combined, though the available turbocharged engine drops to 26 mpg combined. There’s not much of a difference here, but the upcoming hybrid-powered version of the Seltos could tip the scales later this year. The Seltos offers 27.8 cubic feet of cargo capacity behind the second row and up to 64.2 cubic feet with the rear seats folded, putting it among the roomiest vehicles in its class. Front storage is less impressive since the narrow center console is deep but not particularly spacious, but there are plenty of additional compartments for smaller items. The HR-V offers less capacity behind the rear seats at 24.4 cubic feet, but the cargo area is well thought out and makes good use of the space. The rear seatbacks fold nearly flat with the cargo floor, making it easier to haul longer items while expanding total cargo room to 55.1 cubic feet. Cabin storage is adequate, with a rubberized bridge compartment behind the shifter for wireless charging and a deep center-armrest bin, though the door pockets and glovebox are smaller than we’d prefer. The HR-V makes a strong impression with a well-built, thoughtfully designed interior that features soft-touch surfaces and high-quality-feeling controls. It’s also reasonably priced, with the HR-V LX trim starting at $28,150 including destination fees. The HR-V EX-L tops the lineup at $32,000. The Seltos has a lower starting price of $26,485, and while fully loaded trims can approach $40,000, you’re generally getting more for your money here. The Seltos has a bigger standard touchscreen, more available driver aids, and more convenience features — such as a power-adjustable driver’s seat or leather upholstery — at a lower price. Kia also has a significant advantage in warranty coverage, with five years/60,000 miles of basic coverage and 10 years/100,000 miles on the powertrain. • Edmunds says: The Honda HR-V covers the bases for what’s expected from an extra-small SUV. But the redesigned Kia Seltos has raised the bar to an all-new level with its generous passenger and cargo space, range of powertrain options, and appealing value. If you want top versatility and style from a small SUV, the Seltos is the way to go. This story was provided to the Associated Press by the automotive website Edmunds.

title: Sutton's predictions: Everton v Ipswich Town - Yahoo Sports
content: I nearly went for an Ipswich draw last week but changed my mind and went for Crystal Palace to win. That meant I'd predicted Ipswich would lose their first four league games and they are joint-bottom of the table based on my predictions. Gary O'Neil's side have obviously done much better than that in reality - I know Palace went down to 10 men last week but, even so, well done to the Tractor Boys for finding a way to win that game. Fair play to them, I like the ambition the club's owners have shown in the transfer market, and I really like the way O'Neil sets his team up. They are not just there to sit in in games, and they have got their reward. I still fancy Everton to win this, though. They have made a great start to the season to stay unbeaten so far and, under David Moyes, they are a battle-hardened, resolute and well-organised outfit. As a former Norwich striker, I often get accused of being biased against Ipswich, but I am not being overly negative about them here. I just see it being a tough afternoon for them, without getting a goal, and then a long trip home for their fans on the A14 - hopefully they don't close any of the major roads on Saturday so it is not an even more miserable journey back for them.

title: Sutton's predictions: Brighton v Arsenal - Yahoo Sports
content: There might be a bit of an edge to this one after Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler had a pop at Arsenal over their time-wasting when they beat the Seagulls near the end of last season. I love the way Brighton play and I was at Old Trafford to watch their comeback to beat Manchester United in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. It doesn't seem to matter who they are missing from their team, Brighton are just bold as brass with the way they press and get men forward. Luka Vuskovic, who they got from Spurs for £46m in the summer, is only 19 but he strolled through the game against United. What a player he looks. The issue I have with Brighton in this game, however, is that Arsenal are not Manchester United. They are a cut above that. Arsenal are the real deal and I don't see any weaknesses in their team, as their impressive win at Sunderland underlined. They are brave going forward, but they are also streetwise defensively and can see out a game when they have to, time-wasting or not. They have that steel about them but I also think they could expose Brighton if Hurzeler's side go toe-to-toe with them, which is what I am expecting.

Check out 18 facts and figures about Liverpool's trip to face AFC Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday. Matchday five of the campaign sees the Reds visit Vitality Stadium for a 2pm BST kick-off. Opta and LFC statistician Ged Rea have shared the following trivia related to the encounter... Liverpool have completed a league double over the Cherries in six of the last nine seasons when the two teams have met. Joe Gomez's next game will be the 300th appearance of his club career. Liverpool only failed to score in one of their previous 18 Premier League games against Bournemouth. Bournemouth have lost 14 of their 18 Premier League games against Liverpool (won three, drawn one), though all three victories have come at home – 4-3 in December 2016, 1-0 in March 2023, and 3-2 in January 2026. Bournemouth have failed to win any of their four Premier League games this season (drawn three, lost one), despite leading in all of them; only Manchester City in January 2004 and Tottenham Hotspur in both October 2007 and December 2023 have ever gone five successive games in the competition's history of leading and not winning. The Cherries have drawn 13 of their 23 Premier League matches in 2026 (won eight, lost two), the highest ratio by a team in a single year in the history of the English top flight (56.5 per cent). Liverpool have kept clean sheets in each of their last two Premier League games, more than in their previous 13 combined (one). They haven't gone three in a row without conceding since a run of four between May and September 2024. Andoni Iraola is set to face former club Bournemouth for the first time, with this the first time a Liverpool manager has faced one of their former Premier League clubs since March 2015 when Brendan Rodgers won 1-0 against Swansea City. Iraola was in charge of Bournemouth for 127 games in all competitions from 2023 to 2026, winning 48. He won 41 of his 114 fixtures in the Premier League. Reds bosses are unbeaten in seven against former sides (won five, drawn two) since Kenny Dalglish's side lost 2-0 to Newcastle United in April 2012. No side has had more shots on target in the Premier League this season than Bournemouth (24), with their six per game under Marco Rose the most under any of the five managers to take charge of the Cherries in the competition. Marcus Tavernier has scored in four of his last five Premier League appearances for Bournemouth (four goals), having only scored four times in his previous 24 games. Bournemouth are unbeaten in eight Premier League home matches played on a Sunday (won four, drawn four), although their last defeat was by Liverpool (0-4 in January 2024). In Iraola's third away game in charge, Liverpool are looking to win back-to-back away matches in the Premier League, something they only managed twice in the whole of last season (September and February). Of all sides they have faced 15-plus times in the Premier League, only against Wolverhampton Wanderers (79.2 per cent) do the Reds have a better win rate than versus Bournemouth (77.8 per cent – 14/18). Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has faced Liverpool once before in his managerial career, losing 1-0 with RB Leipzig in the 2024-25 Champions League league phase. title: Climate at the Supreme Court: Suncor v. Boulder | (ACOEL) | American College of Environmental Lawyers - JD Supra
content:
During the spring 2026 semester, I taught Climate Change Law and Policy at the Indiana University McKinney School of Law. The last time I taught the class was in 2021 before I joined the Biden Administration. Boy, how times have changed! Because of actions by the current Administration attempting to dismantle EPA’s regulatory authority over greenhouse gases under the Clean Air Act, including most notably the rescission of the Endangerment Finding, a course that in 2021 required six hours on EPA climate programs required less than half that amount in 2026. I expect I will have more work to do in future years, depending on how the legal challenges to these actions are decided. To prepare for the course, I found myself having to learn new material (imagine!). In particular, I focused on the citizen climate suits, especially Juliana v. United States [see Juliana v. United States, 947 F.3d 1159, 1171 (9th Cir. 2020)], and the numerous efforts by state and local governments to seek damages from the fossil fuel industry through litigation or state legislation. My students and I were inspired by the energy and creativity of the States of Hawaii, Connecticut, Vermont, and New York, the cities of New York and Honolulu, and others, struggling to plan and pay for infrastructure and other solutions to protect their residents, institutions, and businesses from flooding, wildfires, sea level rise, extreme heat, and extreme weather—the increasing impacts of our changing climate. But we were also worn down by their continuous court losses. Industry defendants have successfully argued that the Compact Clause, federal pre-emption, the Dormant Commerce Clause, political questions, and the Supremacy Clause preclude states and local governments from bringing tort claims such as nuisance, trespass, or misrepresentation, or constitutional claims under the public trust doctrine. While increasingly acknowledging the undeniability of harm from climate change caused by emissions of greenhouse gases, courts have mostly thrown up their hands at finding a path to give plaintiffs their day in court. In 2018, the city of Boulder and Boulder County sued various oil and gas companies under state tort law alleging that the companies deceived consumers and the public about the climate harms of their products, seeking damages under state common law. After a five-year battle over whether the case should be removed to federal court, the 10th Circuit decided it should not, Board of County Commissioners of Boulder County v. Suncor Energy (U.S.A.) Inc., 25 F.4th 1238 (10th Cir. 2022), and the Supreme Court denied certiorari. 143 S. Ct. 1795 (2023). The state court denied defendants’ motion to dismiss on federal preemption grounds and the Colorado Supreme Court affirmed. 2025 CO 21. This time, the US Supreme Court decided to hear the case, which will be argued on October 5, 2026. In addition to jurisdictional questions, the substantive question presented is whether federal law precludes a local government from seeking damages under state tort law for misleading the public about the damaging effects of greenhouse gas emissions on the global climate. Dozens of briefs have been filed by amici curiae on both sides, all available at the Supreme Court Docket. Despite the increasingly serious real-world impacts on communities across America, dealing meaningfully with climate change has proven to be impossible for the legislative branch and very challenging for the administrative branch given election cycles, litigation, and the overall political toxicity of the issue. With Boulder v Suncor, the US Supreme Court has the opportunity to decide whether those who are suffering injury and monetary loss have the ability to go to court to prove their case and seek damages. ©

title: Cadillac's $168,000 Escalade-V Packs More Horsepower Than An AMG GLS 63 And Undercuts A Rolls-Royce Cullinan - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update Only a few American luxury automakers remain in business, notably Lucid, Lincoln, and Cadillac. The Lucid Gravity SUV is quick and powerful, which one might expect from an EV. Lincoln focuses on being premium, rather than building high-performance models. Only Cadillac brings a body-on-frame SUV with a supercharged V8 to a competition dominated by German and British performance cars. Mercedes-Benz has the AMG GLS 63, Aston Martin offers the 717-horsepower DBX S, and Rolls-Royce even rules the party with its stately Cullinan. All that said, the Escalade-V is the last unapologetically American entry into a segment controlled by European brands. All specs come directly from the manufacturers. Pricing is correct at the time of writing, and excludes destination, options, taxes, incentives, and other potential dealer fees. Automakers reserve the right to change prices at any time without notice. Excluding Cadillac's actual Rolls-Royce rival, the Celestiq, which starts in the low-$400k range, the Escalade-V is the most expensive model Cadillac currently offers. The base 2027 Escalade-V starts at $169,300 before destination and options, while the long-wheelbase ESV begins at $172,300 for its added interior room. That price is a hard pill to swallow when you consider its competition. The 2026 Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 currently starts at $151,050 before options. A customer could add the Executive Rear Seat package, the Manufaktur custom interior package, and a Burmester 29-speaker 3D audio system, and you'd barely reach the Escalade-V's base price. However, both rivals' prices pale in comparison to the Rolls-Royce Cullinan. It's on an entirely different level of luxury and customization. The Rolls isn't a direct rival to the Escalade-V or the AMG GLS 63. Cadillac isn't afraid of the luxury industry's big names, though, as proven by the Celestiq. That said, the Cullinan starts at around $429,600 before options, which helps put the Escalade-V's price into perspective in this segment. Despite being Cadillac's most expensive SUV, it doesn't hold its value all that well. According to CarEdge, the Escalade in general loses about 58% of its value after its first five years on the road. Of course, the V-Series model may hold value slightly better because it's a more desirable performance variant, but real-world listings for used models show significant depreciation. Using CarBuzz's price trend data, we can see the 2023 Escalade-V (the year this variant debuted) is currently worth about $107,000 on average. That figure accounts for 70 listings posted around the country for a fair average, with the highest asking price reaching $151,440. Nicer examples often go to auction, where owners expect to sell for higher reserves. Online auction data shows the Escalade-V averages $124,067. This includes all model years from 2023 to today, so newer, lower-mileage examples are raising its overall average. On that note, CarEdge also has data on the Mercedes-Benz GLS, which it found depreciates by 48% after five years. The AMG GLS 63 variant may hold value better, simply because it's a more desirable high-performance model. Finally, iSeeCars is another trustworthy source, which finds the Rolls-Royce Cullinan will lose about 38.9% of its value in half a decade. All three models are more powerful than any SUV driver needs, but they produce that power and handle differently. Cadillac uses an existing truck platform to build its body-on-frame model, then equips it with the same engine used in the CT5-V Blackwing. It's a 6.2-liter V8 with a supercharger that boosts its output to 682 horsepower and 653 lb-ft of torque. A 10-speed automatic transmission sends power to all four wheels, which provide enough grip to launch the model to 60 mph from a standstill in a claimed 4.4 seconds. It's quick, but not as quick as you think. Cadillac quotes a sprint from zero to 60 mph taking 4.4 seconds. A few unofficial stopwatch sprints got me there in just under 5 seconds, so I don't doubt the official time. Thing is, the Caddy's force-fed V8 has a lot of mass to get moving... - Christopher Smith, Senior Editor, CarBuzz (2025 Cadillac Escalade-V Drive Review) Some characteristics we highlight in our drive review include its brutally loud exhaust, horrible fuel economy of 13 combined mpg, and aggressive road presence from sharper styling than the regular Escalade. It also handles fairly well for a 6,361-pound SUV; when in V-mode, steering is tighter, the six-piston Brembo brakes are more sensitive, and its suspension prevents too much body roll around corners. The AMG GLS 63 is no slouch. It's equipped with a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 that makes 603 horsepower and 627 lb-ft of torque. A nine-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission sends power to all four wheels, which is smooth enough for a claimed 4.1-second 0-60 mph sprint. Then we have the Cullinan. This high-luxury SUV isn't built for speed, but it's not slow, either. Under the hood is a 6.75-liter twin-turbocharged V12 that makes 563 horsepower and 627 lb-ft of torque, and the Black Badge variant pushes 592 hp and 664 lb-ft of torque. The standard model can sprint to 60 mph in about 5.0 seconds before reaching a limited top speed of 155 mph. General Motors' 6.2-liter V8 has major issues that have been plaguing trucks and SUVs, including the Escalade-V, for a few years. There have been lawsuits and recalls, but even the federal government is tired of hearing about it. GM's recalls haven't totally fixed the issues, and bad engines keep coming out of the factory. Nevertheless, buyers keep choosing Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac models like this one. Even if your engine is free of factory machining debris, you'll still be on the hook for luxury SUV-worthy maintenance costs. CarEdge data shows owners are paying an average of $4,803 in maintenance and repair costs over their first five years on the road. That's $1,657 less than the average luxury SUV and beats both the Mercedes-Benz GLS and Rolls-Royce Cullinan by far. The same source notes a 17.65% chance an Escalade could need a major repair, or a repair costing $500 or more, within its first five years on the road. That's 2.9% better than similar vehicles in its segment. CarEdge also says owners spend $5,940 to maintain and repair their GLSs in their first five years of service. AMG variants could cost slightly more, depending on how aggressively owners drive and treat their models. Harder driving could cause parts to break sooner, leading to higher yearly costs. The Cullinan is a little harder to find averages for, since relatively few are on the road. That said, some dealerships publish their anticipated service costs; one dealer explains how an annual service, including an oil change, tire rotation, and inspecting countless other parts, could cost $4,000. Our road tester explains how the engine might be what everybody wants to hear about, but the Escalade-V's interior may be its best feature. JD Power just named Cadillac the most innovative brand selling cars in the United States, as it stands out in five main categories: comfort and convenience, connected vehicle, driver assist, electric vehicle, and smart vehicle. That said, the Escalade-V's comfort and convenience are better than its bold performance. It comes with a 55-inch pillar-to-pillar screen for the gauge cluster, infotainment system, and passenger entertainment, plus two standard 12.6-inch screens for the second-row passengers. Leather and carbon fiber adorn the interior. A 36-speaker AKG surround-sound audio system is standard, along with so much more. The AMG GLS 63 is just as luxurious, with its heated, ventilated, and massaging front seats, among plenty of other features too long to list. Plus, we'd need a whole separate article to write about the Rolls-Royce Cullinan's features. Nevertheless, the Escalade-V's pure American excess is exactly why you should be considering it. A GLS might blend into the crowd, while the Cullinan costs more than twice as much as the Escalade-V. Choosing the Cadillac means having more eyes on you, as your SUV sounds like a Corvette rumbling, popping, and banging when you let off the accelerator. Sources: Cadillac, Mercedes-Benz, Rolls-Royce, CarEdge, iSeeCars, Classic.com We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. They say the Escalade V-Series can go toe-to-toe with the likes of the Mercedes GLS 63 AMG or BMW XB7 Alpina! It looks great, has a fantastic powertrain, and the Escalade has a timeless cool factor. You can forget about Porsche—they’re going all-electric (BEV) now. With the RSQ7 and RSQ8, Audi caters to customers who want a taste of the German dream while in the US—so, not exactly the typical American buyer. Personally, I’m not a fan of SUVs, but if someone wants one, they should go for it—provided they buy or lease it with their own after-tax money. I dislike it when governments around the world subsidize these massive SUVs—whether they’re internal combustion (ICE) or BEVs, which are even bulkier and heavier, making them even more dangerous for smaller cars and pedestrians. title: Dark Lo & V Don Break Down Each Track From ‘Made of Gold’ - Billboard
content:
The underground's dynamic duo make their triumphant return with their first project together since 2023's Charlie Pope 2. I have tweets going back to 2019 comparing Dark Lo and V Don to the likes of Gang Starr, and Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen, because their chemistry is undeniable. In the era of streaming, where every album is 20-30 tracks long and every song is made to be a charting single, these two keep things simple, and in turn have been offering up timeless rap music for nearly 10 years. Take Dark Lo’s 2017 single “Bandana,” for example — the North Philadelphia rapper goes off for nearly seven minutes straight over V Don’s gritty production, as he brings the listener into his world of pain with a unique flow and voice that you won’t be able to hear anywhere else. That was the first track that made me really start paying attention. Since then, they’ve collaborated on about four albums, including the one we’re hear to talk about today just in time for the release of the deluxe version. The duo started working on Made of Gold back in April of 2025 as soon as Dark Lo came home after serving four years of a seven-and-half year sentence stemming from intimidating a witness in the AR-Ab case that saw his close friend and collaborator get sentenced to a staggering 45 years. You can imagine, however, that Lo wasn’t immediately inspired to make music when he got out and it took him some time to get back into the grow of things. “I wrote ‘Freeze Tag’ and chilled for like a month,” he tells me when they stop by Billboard‘s New York City offices. “It wasn’t in me. I didn’t want to go to the studio. I was lightweight depressed on some s—t. Like, I’m home, but I’m on house arrest, I’m broke. It was a lot of s—t.” He’s back in Dark Lo the Crook mode now, though, as he and V Don plan to continue rolling out this project and have another one basically ready to go. “Hopefully, we drop first quarter next year. I just sent him some crazy s—t the other day,” the Harlem producer says after I ask what’s next for them, with the Philly rapper adding that he’s hoping to go on a feature run soon. We kicked it a couple weeks ago before the deluxe dropped today, and they broke down each of the 11 tracks — so you can use this as sort of a companion as you sink your teeth into the four new tracks they added to the original. Check out our conversation below. V Don: I just started sending joints when he got home. I went to go see him like once or twice. We cooked up some joints in person. I sent him a beat called “Made of Gold,” and then it just seemed like perfect for his whole situation. This is the intro track. Why’d you name it ‘”540 Months”? Dark Lo: That’s for my man. They gave him that time. Dark Lo: I say a bar in there like, “They gave my dog 540 months.” There wasn’t supposed to be no hook at first, but I put a little bridge there at the end. Why’d you guys decide to lead with this one? It was the first single, right? V Don: To me, it stood out, especially for his first joint coming back. He was talking on that and the beat is crazy. How’d you come up with the production on this one? V Don: I was looking for samples and I heard them keys on the original record. So, I chopped it up and as soon as I made it, I sent it to Lo because I know it sounded like some s—t he would f—k with. Is this song title in reference to being inside? Because you were talking about some jail s—t in there. Dark Lo: Nah. “Cabin fever” is just my flow. That s—t’s sick. It’s on some s—t like that. If I’m on a song, I’m gonna give you some of everything. I’m gonna give you some jail s—t, some street s—t, I’m gonna give you some pain. Dark Lo: I said that bar because now I be outside like, “That’s a reptilian, I’m huntin’ them.” V Don: That’s probably one of the last tracks we did. Dark Lo: V Don ain’t like that joint. Keep it a bean. I said that gotta go on there. V Don: I was buggin’. You know what it was, though? You started off with the hook, so I just switched it up and started it off with a verse. Now that’s probably my favorite. I’m like that, though. It’ll take me a little minute. V Don: I love that song now. I love the video. All that. When you were inside, were you able to to write raps? Dark Lo: I ain’t write no raps. Not one. I didn’t think about rap while I was inside. I was on other s—t. I was reading, working out. There were jail politics going on.I had no interest in writing raps at while I was locked up. V Don: I felt like we needed something with some some energy too, so that was one of the last records where I felt like it took it there. Talk about some of the s—t you were kickin’ on here. You touched on some jail stuff on here, that’s why I asked if you were able to get some writing done while you were inside. Dark Lo: That’s some of the realest s—t I ever wrote. Just reminiscing, basically. Talking about running around the hood when I was younger. Then at the bridge part at the end, I’m talking about all the s—t that happened to me, that I survived. V Don: On that one, I switched up the beat at the end, so we can could bring the other joint in. I was gonna ask about that. I had Rome over here and said you help with the transitions on Sock It 2 My Pocket. I feel like the transitions and the audio clips have become your calling card. V Don: I’m trying to make it a real album. Make it like a movie, you know. Dark Lo: As an artist, I know exactly what you mean. That’s why I like working with V Don: It be the in between things, the little breakdowns. I try to merge it all together. Dark Lo: Certain artists like that but some don’t. V Don: I like a lot of details in my s—t. At the end of that song, you hear the police raiding. It’s just bringing it to life. Your production style is dark and atmospheric. It’s like you’re building a world and then you got Dark on it sounding like a villain. I believe everything he’s saying. Dark Lo: You better believe it. This s—t real, cousin. And you keep tabs on what clips might fit with whatever it is that you’re working on at the time. Dark Lo: You trying to get the sauce, man. “How’d you get your flow?” [Laughs.] Not trying to get anyone in trouble. Just trying to get into the process. You don’t have to get into super details. V Don: A lot of times, I might catch something and save it for later. For example, the other day I was watching an interview with Terence Crawford, and he kept talking about chaos. I’m like, “Oh s—t, I’m gonna take that for Ransom next year.” Just keep it in the tuck, you know? You have a line on this track about this maybe being your last album. Is that true? Dark Lo: That’s how I was feeling when I wrote that. V Don: You see the comments, they mad at you for that. Dark Lo: I can’t do that now. When I jump in the groove, I just wanna keep working. Next you know, I got three albums in the tuck. That’s just how you was feeling when he sent you this beat? Dark Lo: I remember when he sent me this joint. I was floatin’ while I was writing to this. I was like, “Fast stalked and got ’em/ Contemplated this my last album/ Rollie on, they ain’t think to rob him/ Was in my hood, I tried to fix a problem/ My mans son got killed, they say my youngin’ shot him.” V Don: You gotta bring the saxophone out for that. [Laughs.] V Don: Nah, I always call my man up whenever I feel like it’s needed. Dark Lo: To add a little sauce V Don He went crazy. Corey’s a beast, man. V Don: What you said? “Two tunas for a green pepper?” Dark Lo: “I thought about Hector.” That’s what it is. V Don: When he sent the joint back, then I I found the skit from The Wire. V Don: When OG first came home, he was trying to chill. They still talking about puttin’ work. V Don: He chillin’ and they like, “You still a soldier, right?” Dark Lo: “Chowline” is one of my favorite jawns. And I feel like I’m my own worst critic. I don’t feel like I really did it justice. I could have did better on that. I don’t know. That’s like my top joint on there. And you liked it even more after he added the sax to it? So, this next one. I love the original. It’s lone of my favorite joints from you guys. What made you decide to make a sequel? Because this one takes on a different tone than the first one. This one is more soulful. V Don: Yeah, the first one was harder. This has a different vibe to it. We named it that because the sample sounded like it was saying, “Alive.” Dark killed it on this. It’s a different record. It’s a more positive sound. I wrote in my notes that it’s less aggressive and more soulful than what we would usually hear from you guys. Talk about where you decided to go with it after you first heard this beat. Dark Lo: It’s less aggressive because it’s more personal to me. When it’s more personal to me, it’s gonna get less aggressive. It’s gonna get a little emotional, you know what I mean? Talking about probably grandma or one of my homies or something like staying alive. V Don: Real life s—t. He was talking about drinking green tea on there. Dark Lo: When I first heard that joint, it came in a batch with “540 Months.” At first, I was like, “I’ma f—k this joint up,” but I sitting with it for like a month or two. Like, “I gotta come real on this.” I was a little intimidated by it, but it came out cool. This is another one of my favorites. You kept listening to the instrumental trying to catch the vibe? Dark Lo: Yeah, I would do a song and then I would go back to this one and listen to it again. Like, “Damn, I’m not ready for this one yet.” How do you write? Do you use your phone? Pen and paper? Dark Lo: I use my phone, but when I transitioned, I couldn’t do it at first. I still needed the pen and paper. V Don: Yeah, I love that record too. When he sent that back, I was like, “Damn, this s—t deep.” It’s different from anything you guys have done. It stood out to me. V Don: I got my homegirl Ashli James to throw some vocals at the end during post-production. This one of my favorite ones. Dark is going crazy on this. Dark Lo: That’s the first jawn I did when I came home. Shot the video and everything. V Don: I had that beat for years. I would send it to people, but nobody got on it, so I was glad when he got on it. When I heard this, I was like, “Yeah, we back to work. This sounding like Lo right here.” Did you feel apprehensive about getting back to the music? You didn’t have writer’s block or anything like that? Dark Lo: Nah. I’ma dog, for real. I just got back out there. It wasn’t nothing. Because I seen what was going on in the rap game, so it wan’t nothing to get back out there. This shit smooth jazz, metabolic type joint. It’s really not me, it’s really the beat. V Don: He started it off fire. “I’m ’bout to leave, ya bitch goin’.” You was talking Spanish on that. You said, “Used to sell perico/ Me and Pito.” That has to be a Puerto Rican. Dark Lo: That’s my childhood friend. We lives on the same block. V Don: There’s a bunch of Puerto Ricans in your hood, right? Badlands. Dark Lo: Yeah, North Philly. Little Puerto Rico. You get a little barbecue chicken on the stick. Pinchos. This is the title track. Do you remember making this beat? V Don: I made that a while back too, and I I just be naming the beats like whatever come in my mind, and I just named it, “Made of Gold.” The beat sounded like an interlude to me at first, but I still sent it to him to see what he could come up with, and he bodied it. After he sent it back, I added little stuff to it like some vocals. Dark Lo: When you made of gold, you gotta go through the fire, but it refines you. Gold comes out the dirt and you gotta wash it, then it goes through a fire process. And then when it’s a done product, it’s beautiful. I’m made of gold. I’ve been through all types of s—t. I’m still here, beautiful. That’s why we titled the album this. It was really on some jail s—t too. When it felt like the sun fell, I was sunk in a cell. That’s the process of the gold being in the dirt, going through all types of s—t. But I made it gold, I’m back out. I rose like Jesus. I’m just assuming, but does this have to do with when you were locked up? You had burgers on Wednesdays? Dark Lo: Listen, in the feds, you get burgers every Wednesday. It’s never gonna change. You’re never gonna wake up on a Wednesday and it’s gonna be something different. You get chicken Thursday. Everybody knows when it’s burger day. It’s some fed s—t. Are they good? They let you add little seasonings to it? Dark Lo: They let you bring some cheese. Some BBQ sauce. We got burgers and fries every Wednesday. It’s alright, but you get a little burned out from it. You was in there making the jailhouse meals they be making on social media? Dark Lo: A few of my mans was the cooks in there. I would just give them some stuff and they would make something. Was there anything that they made that was actually pretty good? Dark Lo: They used to make pizza in there. I’m talking about real live pizza with the cheese pull and all that. I’m talking about serious joints, and they would make little rice balls. Serious joints. V Don: I don’t even remember making that to be honest with you, man. But I got surgical on that one. Definitely chopped up the sample crazy. Drums is knockin’. It got some energy to that joint. Dark Lo: I usually write the hook first, but on this on, I just started writing my verses. And then when I said, “Burgers every Wednesday,” I figured we’re just going to name it that. Dark Lo: It’s like an inside jawn for somebody in the feds, ’cause everybody be like, “What’s today, burger?” Why do you think you usually write your hooks first? Dark Lo: I don’t know, man. When I write my hooks, it be the first four to eight bars. I be like, “This the hook right here.” Dark Lo: I might change it up like put something right there or put this right here. But usually, the first eight bars, I just write it like I’m writing a rap, like I’m writing some bars, but then I’ll be like, “Whoa, I’m gonna bring this back after I spit this 32.” That’s how I be doing it. Then I’ll write the rest around the hook. I love this beat, and Dark went off, talking about, “Tuxedo on, I stole the show.” That’s a good ass line. V Don: That’s another joint I had for a minute, but I wouldn’t send it to nobody because I just felt like they probably ain’t gonna see it how I see it. So, I sent it to him, he sent it back, and the s—t was perfect. It’s another one of them jazz type joints. V Don: I made it before he came home. I wasn’t thinking too much of the beat at first. I’m like it’s cool, but I don’t know who’s gonna do it right. He was locked up and you see what he did to it. That’s one of my favorite joints, man. That s—t wavy, so it’s a vibe. V Don: Yeah, definitely. I added that big 808 you here, added little sprinkles and s—t. He said, “Papi, keep callin’,” but I’m like, “Nah, that s—t sound like a hook. Let me chop it up to make it a hook.” Dark Lo: I just felt like…I don’t know if you would agree, but I think this is more aggressive than the last song you said. I was just real like…I felt aggressive. I wanted to say the worst s—t. I don’t know, man, the beat just felt violent. I wanted to say some violent s—t on here, some aggressive s—t, but still some smooth s—t. Some smooth criminal s—t. V Don: That’s the right phrase: smooth criminal. What else you said on there? “I got this tramp with me, I’m like her father.” Dark Lo: Yeah, I performed with Rome, but besides that, I’m still on parole. He ain’t tripping, but we e about to get everything together. You’ll be able to travel and go overseas. I wonder how that crowd is for y’all. I bet they f—k with you. They love this type of rap out there. V Don: Heavy. I’ve been out there twice and it was was all love. I was out there with Willie the Kid last winter. I was in London. They showed us mad love. How did you feel when you first heard this beat? Because I was like, “This is crazy,” when I first heard it. Dark Lo: It was so fire when I heard that s—t, man. I had to go back because I could probably hear a pack, go to another pack and then come back to that first pack the next day and it be some most fire s—t I ever heard. The bars was just coming, “Working out with this water bag/ See how fast five years fly past/ Thank God, then I fast.” V Don: When he did the devil joint on there and changed his voice? That was crazy. Dark Lo: Ain’t no hook on there either. That was just bars. If you’re familiar with my music I’ve used that filter before. Talk about the thought process behind that. What made you want to go with it there? Dark Lo: I just be feeling like sometimes the devil be whispering to me. So, why you named it “2000 Grams”? Any specific reason? V Don: I don’t even know why I named it that. [Laughs.] Dark Lo: It just fit perfectly. I thought about changing the name but that s—t go perfect with the song for some reason. This is probably my favorite line on this entire project. A lot of these younger rappers be talking about running off on the plug. And you said, “We gettin’ money with the plug, we ain’t have to rob him.” Dark Lo:  I’ll probably talk rob the plug s—t, but I never really robbed the plug, I was gettin’ money with him. I’ve dealt with plugs when I was broke and they would put me right back on my feet. I’ll die for this n—a, for real. V Don: You run off and that s—t f—k everything up. And then they’ll tell other plugs like, “This dude ran off on me, don’t trust him.” Dark Lo: They’ll send a n—a like me to go find you. V Don: I think this is one of the ones we did. It kinda gave me a Mobb Deep feel when I was working on it. I added some more stuff to it after he sent it back. Another hard record, it just sounded right to close the album up with this one. You guys plan on working together again? You said this might be your last album. You was in your feelings. [Laughs.] Dark Lo: It’s too late now. I got albums done. I was definitely in my feelings. How long did you guys take to put this project together? Dark Lo: Like I said, he sent me beats first day I came home, but it took me a minute to really get back to it. I came home April of last year. I had to chill for a minute until the time was right. I’m that type of person. I let the energy and the vibe and mood come to me. If I don’t feel it, I ain’t feeling it. V Don: We were basically done with the album the end last year, but we wanted to get all the assets ready, we shout some videos. Made sure we had everything together. Word, start rolling it out. And then you come home the economy’s all weird and s—t. Groceries expensive as hell. Dark Lo: Now they cut you off., bro, I went to the market… I be having to remember to use the app and pick out coupons to add to the keychain card. title: Honda Reportedly Fast-Tracks Next-Gen CR-V, More Hybrids After Killing EVs - Road & Track
content: A new report suggests the next CR-V will begin production in early 2027. Honda took the axe to its whole EV operation earlier this year, leaving it with a few holes in its lineup. Now, it could be fast-tracking the development and launch of next-generation hybrid vehicles, starting with the CR-V. As reported by Nikkei, Honda is moving up the launch and production of its next-gen CR-V to February 2027. The current model isn’t especially old, considering it went on sale in late 2022 as a 2023 model year vehicle. That said, it’s Honda’s most popular vehicle here in the U.S., so keeping it competitive with other hybrid compact SUVs like the Toyota RAV4 (now hybrid-only) is vital. Nikkei reports that the CR-V that launches next year will be a full redesign of the current model. It’s set to be fitted with Honda’s next-generation hybrid technology, which we suspect will be an evolution of the company’s two-motor hybrid system it’s used for years. The report doesn’t specify whether or not this CR-V will be hybrid-only or continue to offer a purely gas-powered variant, but we wouldn’t be surprised to see Honda follow in Toyota’s footsteps and go all-in on its excellent hybrid powertrain. In addition to this Honda news, the report says Acura will launch a new hybrid vehicle based on this next-gen CR-V. The RDX has long been Acura’s CR-V-like SUV offering in terms of size and use case. However, Acura said in January that the next RDX was “planned for market introduction in the next couple of years,” suggesting it will launch much later than this next-gen CR-V. We already knew Honda was developing a three-row hybrid SUV based on previous reports, but this latest report from Nikkei further confirms the presence of such a vehicle. The plan would be for that model to launch in 2029. Instead of the four-cylinder two-motor hybrid powertrain, a V-6-based two-motor hybrid system is reportedly being developed that would power this large hybrid vehicle. Road & Track reached out to Honda about this report and received the following statement in response. “This was not announced by Honda. While we cannot comment on specific future product plans, as outlined in our 2026 Business Update, Honda remains on track to introduce next-generation HEV models beginning in 2027, featuring an all-new hybrid system and platform.” We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we back.

title: V GIRLS: Freya Skye Is Writing Her Way Into Who She Is Becoming - V Magazine
content: At 16, Freya Skye is only beginning to see where the road might take her, with music as her north star. At 16, Freya Skye is only beginning to see where the road might take her, with music as her north star. Freya Skye was five years old when a karaoke machine appeared under the Christmas tree, and she has been singing ever since. At 13, she represented the UK at the Junior Eurovision Song Contest. By now, at 16, she has amassed over 2.5 billion streams and sold out more than a hundred shows worldwide. She also released a debut EP in February called Stardust that charted in both the US and UK. “I don’t really believe in coincidences,” she says of that first karaoke machine. “Music has always had a way of finding me or maybe I’ve always had a way of finding it.” Skye created Stardust with some of pop’s most in-demand names — like songwriter Julia Michaels and Grammy-winning producers Mattman and Robin, known for their work with Selena Gomez and Taylor Swift — but the songs are unmistakably hers. “Each song is a piece of who I was when I wrote it,” she says. “They’re messy, honest, and a little bit broken on their own but together they tell the full story.” Lead single “silent treatment,” about being ghosted without explanation, has clocked over 100M streams across all DSPs.”It’s not a hyper-specific story, it’s a specific feeling,” she says. “Everyone has been on one side of that silence or the other.” Writing with Michaels left a mark that went beyond the songs. “She’s so calm and grounded, genuinely kind to write with, and within ten minutes she knew everything about me because I’m an open book like that,” Skye says. “When someone that secure in themselves is sitting across from you, you end up writing braver.” Her shows have grown from 200-capacity rooms to 7,000-seat venues in under a year, and she has fought hard to keep them accessible — partnering with Ticketmaster to ensure her tour tickets can only be resold at face value. “Keeping tickets as affordable as possible is so important, especially with my fanbase where we’re all teenagers and young girls,” she says. “You never want to close people out.” The devotion goes both ways. “They’ve been queuing since seven that morning, dressed up, giving everything they have. I’m just giving it back to them.” Freya Skye’s latest single ‘Bad Taste’ arrived September 16 and is now available to stream across all platforms as she continues work on her debut album. Her film Zombies 5: Secrets of the Sea, in which she plays Nova, is now in production. Her world is only getting bigger, fashion included. In July, Hollister named her the face of its fall “Made for This Moment” denim campaign, a partnership that will also see the brand sponsor her upcoming tour dates across North America, the UK and Europe. She wears it all lightly: the Oscar de la Renta gown she wore at the Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires premiere made her feel “like a completely different, more grown-up version of myself for a night,” she says, though at home she’s happiest in “the comfiest thing I own, some huge hoodie.” Wherever it all goes next, Skye says, she’s ready for it, because her passion remains: “Music is the part of me I can never turn off.” This cover story appears in the pages of V162: now available for purchase!
